sourceDependency: DUB-17 frozen Theorem 2.6 / DUB-18 Corollary 8.2 -> symmetric-power continuation -> arithmetic automorphy -> residual Galois association -> original parabolic Hecke realization -> period surjectivity -> matching cusp-form lower dimension bound -> regular differential dimension -> finite original canonical-divisor space and its linear equivalence with regular differentials.
routeAdjustment: Use the already proved positive-order degree identity to identify the constants, avoiding a new rational-place existence framework. Select only the local residue-map kernel from the external finite-divisor-space argument, and use the pinned finite-submodule quotient theorem plus finite-pole induction. This proves finiteness without porting the external general adele quotient machinery. Adapt the selected canonical-space/regular-differential equivalence and assemble it on the literal original field and its actual j divisor. The Riemann--Roch equality is not used or claimed.
discharged: The actual original regular differential space is finite-dimensional over algebraically closed constants. The positive-order degree formula applied to an inverse forces every transcendental function to have a pole, so global regular functions are exactly the constants. At each place the kernel of the scaled local residue map is the divisor space with its bound decreased by one. Pinned finite-submodule/quotient theory and induction over the positive part of the actual finite divisor prove every divisor space finite. The actual j-canonical divisor space is explicitly linearly equivalent to the actual regular differential space. No constant-field or divisor-space finiteness assumption remains in the original consumer.
remaining: Riemann--Roch and the geometric genus formula still determine the numerical dimension; actual analytic cusp-form realization is also required for the matching lower bound. Period surjectivity, Hecke/Galois realization, the adic system and symmetric-power continuation remain open. DUB-17--20 OPEN; 16/20.
